# globset - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/globset/^0.4.18/

## Expand description

The globset crate provides cross platform single glob and glob set matching.

Glob set matching is the process of matching one or more glob patterns against a single candidate path simultaneously, and returning all of the globs that matched. For example, given this set of globs:

- `*.rs`
- `src/lib.rs`
- `src/**/foo.rs`

and a path `src/bar/baz/foo.rs`, then the set would report the first and third
globs as matching.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-one-glob)Example: one glob

This example shows how to match a single glob against a single file path.

```
use globset::Glob;
let glob = Glob::new("*.rs")?.compile_matcher();
assert!(glob.is_match("foo.rs"));
assert!(glob.is_match("foo/bar.rs"));
assert!(!glob.is_match("Cargo.toml"));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#example-configuring-a-glob-matcher)Example: configuring a glob matcher

This example shows how to use a `GlobBuilder` to configure aspects of match
semantics. In this example, we prevent wildcards from matching path separators.

```
use globset::GlobBuilder;
let glob = GlobBuilder::new("*.rs")
    .literal_separator(true).build()?.compile_matcher();
assert!(glob.is_match("foo.rs"));
assert!(!glob.is_match("foo/bar.rs")); // no longer matches
assert!(!glob.is_match("Cargo.toml"));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#example-match-multiple-globs-at-once)Example: match multiple globs at once

This example shows how to match multiple glob patterns at once.

```
use globset::{Glob, GlobSetBuilder};
let mut builder = GlobSetBuilder::new();
// A GlobBuilder can be used to configure each glob's match semantics
// independently.
builder.add(Glob::new("*.rs")?);
builder.add(Glob::new("src/lib.rs")?);
builder.add(Glob::new("src/**/foo.rs")?);
let set = builder.build()?;
assert_eq!(set.matches("src/bar/baz/foo.rs"), vec![0, 2]);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#syntax)Syntax

Standard Unix-style glob syntax is supported:

- `?`matches any single character. (If the- `literal_separator`option is enabled, then- `?`can never match a path separator.)
- `*`matches zero or more characters. (If the- `literal_separator`option is enabled, then- `*`can never match a path separator.)
- `**`recursively matches directories but are only legal in three situations. First, if the glob starts with- `**/`, then it matches all directories. For example,- `**/foo`matches- `foo`and- `bar/foo`but not- `foo/bar`. Secondly, if the glob ends with- `/**`, then it matches all sub-entries. For example,- `foo/**`matches- `foo/a`and- `foo/a/b`, but not- `foo`. Thirdly, if the glob contains- `/**/`anywhere within the pattern, then it matches zero or more directories. Using- `**`anywhere else is illegal (N.B. the glob- `**`is allowed and means “match everything”).
- `{a,b}`matches- `a`or- `b`where- `a`and- `b`are arbitrary glob patterns. (N.B. Nesting- `{...}`is not currently allowed.)
- `[ab]`matches- `a`or- `b`where- `a`and- `b`are characters. Use- `[!ab]`to match any character except for- `a`and- `b`.
- Metacharacters such as `*`and`?`can be escaped with character class notation. e.g.,`[*]`matches`*`.
- When backslash escapes are enabled, a backslash (`\`) will escape all meta characters in a glob. If it precedes a non-meta character, then the slash is ignored. A`\\`will match a literal`\\`. Note that this mode is only enabled on Unix platforms by default, but can be enabled on any platform via the`backslash_escape`setting on`Glob`.

A `GlobBuilder` can be used to prevent wildcards from matching path separators,
or to enable case insensitive matching.

[§](https://docs.rs#crate-features)Crate Features

This crate includes optional features that can be enabled if necessary. These features are not required but may be useful depending on the use case.

The following features are available:

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Candidate](https://docs.rs/struct.Candidate.html)
- A candidate path for matching.
- [Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Error.html)
- Represents an error that can occur when parsing a glob pattern.
- [Glob](https://docs.rs/struct.Glob.html)
- Glob represents a successfully parsed shell glob pattern.
- [Glob](https://docs.rs/struct.GlobBuilder.html)- Builder
- A builder for a pattern.
- [Glob](https://docs.rs/struct.GlobMatcher.html)- Matcher
- A matcher for a single pattern.
- [GlobSet](https://docs.rs/struct.GlobSet.html)
- GlobSet represents a group of globs that can be matched together in a single pass.
- [Glob](https://docs.rs/struct.GlobSetBuilder.html)- SetBuilder
- GlobSetBuilder builds a group of patterns that can be used to simultaneously match a file path.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.ErrorKind.html)- Kind
- The kind of error that can occur when parsing a glob pattern.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [escape](https://docs.rs/fn.escape.html)
- Escape meta-characters within the given glob pattern.

# percent_encoding - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/percent-encoding/^2.3.2/

## Expand description

URLs use special characters to indicate the parts of the request.
For example, a `?` question mark marks the end of a path and the start of a query string.
In order for that character to exist inside a path, it needs to be encoded differently.

Percent encoding replaces reserved characters with the `%` escape character
followed by a byte value as two hexadecimal digits.
For example, an ASCII space is replaced with `%20`.

When encoding, the set of characters that can (and should, for readability) be left alone
depends on the context.
The `?` question mark mentioned above is not a separator when used literally
inside of a query string, and therefore does not need to be encoded.
The [ AsciiSet](https://docs.rs/struct.AsciiSet.html) parameter of

[and](https://docs.rs/fn.percent_encode.html)

`percent_encode`[lets callers configure this.](https://docs.rs/fn.utf8_percent_encode.html)

`utf8_percent_encode`This crate deliberately does not provide many different sets.
Users should consider in what context the encoded string will be used,
read relevant specifications, and define their own set.
This is done by using the `add` method of an existing set.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use percent_encoding::{utf8_percent_encode, AsciiSet, CONTROLS};
/// https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#fragment-percent-encode-set
const FRAGMENT: &AsciiSet = &CONTROLS.add(b' ').add(b'"').add(b'<').add(b'>').add(b'`');
assert_eq!(utf8_percent_encode("foo <bar>", FRAGMENT).to_string(), "foo%20%3Cbar%3E");
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Ascii](https://docs.rs/struct.AsciiSet.html)- Set
- Represents a set of characters or bytes in the ASCII range.
- [Percent](https://docs.rs/struct.PercentDecode.html)- Decode
- The return type of `percent_decode`
- [Percent](https://docs.rs/struct.PercentEncode.html)- Encode
- The return type of `percent_encode``utf8_percent_encode`

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [CONTROLS](https://docs.rs/constant.CONTROLS.html)
- The set of 0x00 to 0x1F (C0 controls), and 0x7F (DEL).
- [NON_](https://docs.rs/constant.NON_ALPHANUMERIC.html)- ALPHANUMERIC
- Everything that is not an ASCII letter or digit.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [percent_](https://docs.rs/fn.percent_decode.html)- decode
- Percent-decode the given bytes.
- [percent_](https://docs.rs/fn.percent_decode_str.html)- decode_ - str
- Percent-decode the given string.
- [percent_](https://docs.rs/fn.percent_encode.html)- encode
- Percent-encode the given bytes with the given set.
- [percent_](https://docs.rs/fn.percent_encode_byte.html)- encode_ - byte
- Return the percent-encoding of the given byte.
- [utf8_](https://docs.rs/fn.utf8_percent_encode.html)- percent_ - encode
- Percent-encode the UTF-8 encoding of the given string.

# id in zrx_id - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/zrx-id/0.0.21/zrx_id/macro.id.html

```
macro_rules! id {
    ($from:expr; $($key:ident = $value:expr),* $(,)?) => { ... };
    ($($key:ident = $value:expr),* $(,)?) => { ... };
    (@set $builder:ident, provider, $value:expr) => { ... };
    (@set $builder:ident, resource, $value:expr) => { ... };
    (@set $builder:ident, variant, $value:expr) => { ... };
    (@set $builder:ident, context, $value:expr) => { ... };
    (@set $builder:ident, location, $value:expr) => { ... };
    (@set $builder:ident, fragment, $value:expr) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Creates an identifier.

This macro creates an [ Id](https://docs.rs/struct.Id.html) from the given key-value pairs, offering a
shorter syntax compared to using the

[directly. Additionally, it allows to create a new identifier based on an existing one by passing it as the first argument.](https://docs.rs/struct.Id.html#method.builder)

`Id::builder`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

Create identifier:

```
use zrx_id::id;
// Create identifier
let id = id!(provider = "file", context = "docs", location = "index.md")?;
assert_eq!(id.as_str(), "zri:file:::docs:index.md:");
```
Create identifier from existing identifier:

```
use zrx_id::{id, Id};
// Create identifier from string
let id: Id = "zri:file:::docs:index.md:".parse()?;
// Create identifier from existing identifier
let id = id!(id; location = "README.md")?;
assert_eq!(id.as_str(), "zri:file:::docs:README.md:");
```

---

# selector in zrx_id - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/zrx-id/0.0.21/zrx_id/macro.selector.html

```
macro_rules! selector {
    ($from:expr; $($key:ident = $value:expr),* $(,)?) => { ... };
    ($($key:ident = $value:expr),* $(,)?) => { ... };
    (@set $builder:ident, provider, $value:expr) => { ... };
    (@set $builder:ident, resource, $value:expr) => { ... };
    (@set $builder:ident, variant, $value:expr) => { ... };
    (@set $builder:ident, context, $value:expr) => { ... };
    (@set $builder:ident, location, $value:expr) => { ... };
    (@set $builder:ident, fragment, $value:expr) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Creates an selector.

This macro creates a [ Selector](https://docs.rs/struct.Selector.html) from the given key-value pairs, offering
a shorter syntax compared to using the

[directly. It also allows to create a new selector based on an existing one by passing it as the first argument.](https://docs.rs/struct.Selector.html#method.builder)

`Selector::builder`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

Create selector:

```
use zrx_id::selector;
// Create selector
let selector = selector!(location = "**/*.md")?;
assert_eq!(selector.as_str(), "zrs:::::**/*.md:");
```
Create selector from existing selector:

```
use zrx_id::{selector, Selector};
// Create selector from string
let selector: Selector = "zrs:::::**/*.md:".parse()?;
// Create selector from existing selector
let selector = selector!(selector; provider = "file")?;
assert_eq!(selector.as_str(), "zrs:file::::**/*.md:");
```

---

# Expression in zrx_id - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/zrx-id/0.0.21/zrx_id/struct.Expression.html

`pub struct Expression { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Expression.

Expressions allow to build trees of [ Id](https://docs.rs/struct.Id.html) and

[instances combined with logical operators, enabling complex matching and filtering.](https://docs.rs/struct.Selector.html)

`Selector`The following operators are supported:

- `Expression::any`- `OR`- any operand must match.
- `Expression::all`- `AND`- all operands must match.
- `Expression::not`- `NOT`- no operand must match.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use zrx_id::{selector, Expression};
// Create expression
let expr = Expression::all(|expr| {
    expr.with(selector!(location = "**/*.md")?)?
        .with(Expression::not(|expr| {
            expr.with(selector!(provider = "file")?)
        })
    )
})?;
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/zrx_id/id/expression/builder.rs.html#49-157)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-Expression)### impl [Expression](https://docs.rs/struct.Expression.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/zrx_id/id/expression/builder.rs.html#49-157)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-Expression)

### impl [Expression](https://docs.rs/struct.Expression.html)

Creates an expression for which any operand must match.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

Returns [ Error::Id](https://docs.rs/expression/enum.Error.html#variant.Id) if any of the operands are invalid.

use zrx_id::{selector, Expression};

    expr.with(selector!(location = "**/*.jpg")?)?
        .with(selector!(location = "**/*.png")?)
})?;
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/zrx_id/id/expression.rs.html#176-203)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-Default-for-Expression)### impl [Default](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/default/trait.Default.html) for [Expression](https://docs.rs/struct.Expression.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/zrx_id/id/expression.rs.html#176-203)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-Default-for-Expression)

### impl [Default](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/default/trait.Default.html) for [Expression](https://docs.rs/struct.Expression.html)

Creates an expression that matches everything.

While it may seem counterintuitive to have the default expression match everything, it is designed this way to align with the concept of vacuous truth in logic. An expression with no operands is considered to be true, as there are no conditions to violate it.

In our implementation, we use an empty expression with a logical `NOT`
operator to represent this concept, to be distinguishable as a marker.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-4)Examples

```
use zrx_id::Expression;
// Create empty expression
let expr = Expression::default();
assert!(expr.is_empty());
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/zrx_id/id/expression.rs.html#78)

### impl [IntoIterator](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/collect/trait.IntoIterator.html) for [Expression](https://docs.rs/struct.Expression.html)

Creates a consuming iterator over the expression.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-5)Examples

```
use zrx_id::{selector, Expression};
// Create expression
let expr = Expression::any(|expr| {
    expr.with(selector!(location = "**/*.jpg")?)?
        .with(selector!(location = "**/*.png")?)
})?;
// Create iterator over expression
for operand in expr {
    println!("{operand:?}");
}
```

#### fn [to_specificity](https://docs.rs/specificity/trait.ToSpecificity.html#tymethod.to_specificity)(&self) -> [Specificity](https://docs.rs/struct.Specificity.html)

Computes the specificity of the expression.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-6)Examples

```
use zrx_id::specificity::ToSpecificity;
use zrx_id::{selector, Expression};
// Create expression and compute specificity
let expr = Expression::any(|expr| {
    expr.with(selector!(location = "**/*.jpg")?)?
        .with(selector!(location = "**/*.png")?)
})?;
assert_eq!(expr.to_specificity(), (0, 1, 1, 4).into());
```

# Id in zrx_id - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/zrx-id/0.0.21/zrx_id/struct.Id.html

`pub struct Id { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Identifier.

Identifiers are structured string-based representations which are used to uniquely identify artifacts as they move through streams and stores. They use a compact, yet human-readable format that is easy to generate and parse, and consists of the following six components:

- `provider`, e.g., file or git.
- `resource`, e.g., volume, branch or tag.
- `variant`, e.g., language, version or format.
- `context`, e.g., source or output directory.
- `location`, e.g., file or folder.
- `fragment`, e.g., line number or anchor.

Identifiers implement [ Eq](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cmp/trait.Eq.html),

[and](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cmp/trait.PartialEq.html)

`PartialEq`[, as well as](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/hash/trait.Hash.html)

`Hash`[and](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cmp/trait.Ord.html)

`Ord`[, so they can be stored in ordered and unordered storages, as well as efficiently compared with each other. The structured string-based representation is defined as follows:](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cmp/trait.PartialOrd.html)

`PartialOrd``zri:<provider>:<resource>:<variant>:<context>:<location>:<fragment>`This ensures blazing fast cloning and editing. Additionally, identifiers are guaranteed to not contain backslashes or path traversals in components. An empty component, for those that are allowed to remain empty, is equal to the default in the context set by the given provider.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

Create an identifier:

```
use zrx_id::Id;
// Create identifier builder
let builder = Id::builder()
    .provider("file")
    .context("docs")
    .location("index.md");
// Create identifier from builder
let id = builder.build()?;
assert_eq!(id.as_str(), "zri:file:::docs:index.md:");
```
Create an identifier from a string:

```
use zrx_id::Id;
// Create identifier from string
let id: Id = "zri:file:::docs:index.md:".parse()?;
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/zrx_id/id/builder.rs.html#94-98)#### pub fn [to_builder](https://docs.rs#method.to_builder)(&self) -> [Builder](https://docs.rs/struct.Builder.html)<'_>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/zrx_id/id/builder.rs.html#94-98)

#### pub fn [to_builder](https://docs.rs#method.to_builder)(&self) -> [Builder](https://docs.rs/struct.Builder.html)<'_>

Creates a builder from the identifier.

This method creates a builder from the current identifier, which allows to modify components and build a new identifier from an existing one.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-2)Examples

```
use zrx_id::Id;
// Create identifier from string
let id: Id = "zri:file:::docs:index.md:".parse()?;
// Create identifier builder
let builder = id.to_builder().location("README.md");
// Create identifier from builder
let id = builder.build()?;
assert_eq!(id.as_str(), "zri:file:::docs:README.md:");
```
Converts the identifier to a relative file system path.

This method creates a relative [ PathBuf](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.PathBuf.html) from both, the

`context` and
`location` components of the identifier, using platform-dependent path
separators. The resulting path is always relative, and never absolute,
since both, `context` and `location`, are always relative.In order to resolve the path, the [ Id::resource](https://docs.rs/struct.Id.html#method.resource) needs to be taken
into account, which is of course provider-specific. Note that for use
of paths in URLs,

[must be used, which guarantees that all path separators are forward slashes.](https://docs.rs/struct.Id.html#method.as_uri)

`Id::as_uri`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-3)Examples

```
use std::path::Path;
use zrx_id::Id;
// Create identifier from string
let id: Id = "zri:file:::docs:index.md:".parse()?;
// Create path from identifier
let path = id.to_path();
assert_eq!(path, Path::new("docs/index.md"));
```
Returns the string representation.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-4)Examples

```
use zrx_id::Id;
// Create identifier from string
let id: Id = "zri:file:::docs:index.md:".parse()?;
// Obtain string representation
assert_eq!(id.as_str(), "zri:file:::docs:index.md:");
```
Returns the URI representation.

This method creates a URI from [ Id::location](https://docs.rs/struct.Id.html#method.location), which is necessary for
using the identifier in URLs, e.g., to construct relative links.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-5)Examples

```
use zrx_id::uri::Uri;
use zrx_id::Id;
// Create identifier from string
let id: Id = "zri:file:::docs:index.md:".parse()?;
// Obtain URI representation
assert_eq!(id.as_uri(), Uri::from("index.md"));
```
## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

Returns the formatted string.

Note that it’s normally not necessary to access the formatted string
directly, as all components can be accessed via the respective methods.
We need to access the underlying formatted string in our internal APIs,
e.g., to compute the [ Specificity](https://docs.rs/struct.Specificity.html) for the given

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Id.html)

`Id`[Source](https://docs.rs/src/zrx_id/id.rs.html#400)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-Eq-for-Id)

Attempts to create an identifier from a string.

The string must adhere to the following format and include exactly six
`:` separators, even in case some components are omitted. The optional
components are `resource`, `variant` and `fragment`, and can be left
empty, which is represented as empty strings internally.

`zri:<provider>:<resource>:<variant>:<context>:<location>:<fragment>`[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

Returns [ Error::Component](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html#variant.Component) if any of the

`provider`, `context` or
`location` components are not set, and [if the prefix isn’t](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html#variant.Prefix)

`Error::Prefix``zri`. On low-level format errors, [is returned.](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html#variant.Format)

`Error::Format`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-6)Examples

```
use zrx_id::Id;
// Create identifier from string
let id: Id = "zri:file:::docs:index.md:".parse()?;
```
Hashes the identifier.

Since identifiers are immutable, we can use a precomputed hash for fast hashing. This is especially useful when identifiers are used as keys in hash maps or hash sets, where hashing is a frequent operation, as the performance gains are significant with constant time.

#### fn [to_specificity](https://docs.rs/specificity/trait.ToSpecificity.html#tymethod.to_specificity)(&self) -> [Specificity](https://docs.rs/struct.Specificity.html)

Computes the specificity of the identifier.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-10)Examples

```
use zrx_id::id;
use zrx_id::specificity::ToSpecificity;
// Create identifier and compute specificity
let id = id!(provider = "file", context = ".", location = "index.md")?;
assert_eq!(id.to_specificity(), (3, 0, 0, 13).into());
```
Attempts to create a selector from an identifier.

An [ Id](https://docs.rs/struct.Id.html) can be converted into a

[because all identifiers are also valid selectors, as they represent exact matches. However, the reverse is not true, as selectors can contain wildcards, as well as optional components, which identifiers cannot.](https://docs.rs/struct.Selector.html)

`Selector`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-11)Examples

```
use zrx_id::{Id, Selector};
// Create selector from identifier
let id: Id = "zri:file:::docs:index.md:".parse()?;
let selector: Selector = id.try_into()?;
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/zrx_id/id/selector/convert.rs.html#73-98)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-TryToSelector-for-Id)### impl [TryToSelector](https://docs.rs/trait.TryToSelector.html) for [Id](https://docs.rs/struct.Id.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/zrx_id/id/selector/convert.rs.html#73-98)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-TryToSelector-for-Id)

### impl [TryToSelector](https://docs.rs/trait.TryToSelector.html) for [Id](https://docs.rs/struct.Id.html)

Attempts to convert to a selector.

Since all identifiers are also valid selectors, implementing this trait
ensures we can also pass identifier references to [ Builder::add](https://docs.rs/matcher/struct.Builder.html#method.add).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-12)Examples

```
use zrx_id::{Id, Selector, TryToSelector};
// Create selector from identifier
let id: Id = "zri:file:::docs:index.md:".parse()?;
let selector = id.try_to_selector()?;
```

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-14)Examples

```

let item: &mut dyn Any = &mut storage;
// Obtain mutable storage reference
let storage = <i32>::try_as_storage_mut(item)?;
```

# Selector in zrx_id - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/zrx-id/0.0.21/zrx_id/struct.Selector.html

`pub struct Selector { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Selector.

Selectors are used to match identifiers. Like identifiers, they consist of
six components, which can be set to specific values or left empty to act as
wildcards. Each component can be set to a glob as supported by [ globset](https://docs.rs/globset/0.4.18/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/globset/index.html),
which allows for powerful matching capabilities.

Selectors are no means to an end, but rather a building block to associate
data or functions to identifiers via the construction of a [ Matcher](https://docs.rs/matcher/struct.Matcher.html),
which uses an efficient algorithm to match an arbitrary set of selectors in
linear time. While it’s recommended to use

[together with the associated methods to create a new selector, selectors can also be created from a structured string representation with](https://docs.rs/struct.Selector.html#method.builder)

`Selector::builder`[, which is used internally for serializing them to persistent storage:](https://docs.rs/struct.Selector.html#method.from_str)

`Selector::from_str``zrs:<provider>:<resource>:<variant>:<context>:<location>:<fragment>`This ensures blazing fast cloning and editing. Additionally, selectors are guaranteed to not contain backslashes or path traversals in components. An empty component is interpreted as a wildcard, and thus matches all values in that component for any given selector.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

Create a selector:

```
use zrx_id::Selector;
// Create selector builder
let builder = Selector::builder().location("**/*.md");
// Create selector from builder
let selector = builder.build()?;
assert_eq!(selector.as_str(), "zrs:::::**/*.md:");
```
Create a selector from a string:

```
use zrx_id::Selector;
// Create selector from string
let selector: Selector = "zrs:::::**/*.md:".parse()?;
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/zrx_id/id/selector/builder.rs.html#95-99)#### pub fn [to_builder](https://docs.rs#method.to_builder)(&self) -> [Builder](https://docs.rs/selector/struct.Builder.html)<'_>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/zrx_id/id/selector/builder.rs.html#95-99)

#### pub fn [to_builder](https://docs.rs#method.to_builder)(&self) -> [Builder](https://docs.rs/selector/struct.Builder.html)<'_>

Creates a builder from the selector.

This method creates a builder from the current selector, which allows to modify components and build a new selector from an existing one.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-2)Examples

```
use zrx_id::Selector;
// Create selector from string
let selector: Selector = "zrs:::::**/*.md:".parse()?;
// Create selector builder
let builder = selector.to_builder().location("index.md");
// Create selector from builder
let selector = builder.build()?;
assert_eq!(selector.as_str(), "zrs:::::index.md:");
```
## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

Returns the formatted string.

Note that it’s normally not necessary to access the formatted string
directly, as all components can be accessed via the respective methods.
We need to access the underlying formatted string in our internal APIs,
e.g., to compute the [ Specificity](https://docs.rs/struct.Specificity.html) for the given

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Selector.html)

`Selector`[Source](https://docs.rs/src/zrx_id/id/selector.rs.html#375)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-Eq-for-Selector)

Attempts to create a selector from a string.

The string must adhere to the following format and include exactly six
`:` separators, even if some components are empty. All components are
optional, which means they can be left empty, which is equivalent to
setting them to a `**` wildcard.

`zrs:<provider>:<resource>:<variant>:<context>:<location>:<fragment>`[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

Returns [ Error::Prefix](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html#variant.Prefix) if the prefix isn’t

`zrs`. Low-level format
errors are returned as part of [.](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html#variant.Format)

`Error::Format`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-4)Examples

```
use zrx_id::Selector;
// Create selector from string
let selector: Selector = "zrs:::::**/*.md:".parse()?;
```
Hashes the selector.

Since selectors are immutable, we can use a precomputed hash for fast hashing. This is especially useful when selectors are used as keys in hash maps or hash sets, where hashing is a frequent operation, as the performance gains are significant.

# Sequence in zrx_id - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/zrx-id/0.0.21/zrx_id/struct.Sequence.html

`pub struct Sequence { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Sequence.

Sequences are ordered collections of expressions that can be used to match identifiers. Sequences can contain gaps, which allow to implement flexible matching of identifiers with varying numbers of elements, including but not limited to prefix and suffix matching.

Each [ Element](https://docs.rs/sequence/enum.Element.html) of a

[can either be an](https://docs.rs/struct.Sequence.html)

`Sequence`[or a](https://docs.rs/struct.Expression.html)

`Expression`[. An](https://docs.rs/sequence/enum.Element.html#variant.Gap)

`Gap`[is a logical combination of one or multiple](https://docs.rs/struct.Expression.html)

`Expression`[and](https://docs.rs/struct.Id.html)

`Id`[instances, while a](https://docs.rs/struct.Selector.html)

`Selector`[represents a wildcard that can match any number of elements, including zero.](https://docs.rs/sequence/enum.Element.html#variant.Gap)

`Gap`The following convenience constructors are provided:

- `Sequence::prefix`
- `Sequence::suffix`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use zrx_id::{selector, Sequence};
// Create sequence
let sequence = Sequence::from([
    selector!(location = "zensical.toml")?,
    selector!(location = "**/*.md")?,
]);
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Creates a sequence where the given elements are a prefix.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-1)Examples

```
use zrx_id::{selector, Sequence};
// Create sequence for a prefix
let sequence = Sequence::prefix([
    selector!(location = "zensical.toml")?,
]);
```
Creates a sequence where the given elements are a suffix.

```

// Create sequence for a suffix

    selector!(location = "**/*.md")?,

```

    selector!(location = "**/*.md")?,

Attempts to convert into a storage reference.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

The following errors might be returned:

- `Error::Downcast`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-13)Examples

```
use std::any::Any;
use zrx_storage::convert::TryAsStorage;
use zrx_storage::Storage;
// Create storage and initial state
let mut storage = Storage::default();
storage.insert("key", 42);
// Obtain type-erased reference
let item: &dyn Any = &storage;
// Obtain storage reference
let storage = <i32>::try_as_storage(item)?;
```

# Specificity in zrx_id - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/zrx-id/0.0.21/zrx_id/struct.Specificity.html

`pub struct Specificity(/* private fields */);`## Expand description

Specificity.

Specificity is an ordering and tie-breaking concept borrowed from CSS, where
more specific selectors take precedence over less specific ones. Specificity
is computable for the likes of [ Expression](https://docs.rs/struct.Expression.html),

[,](https://docs.rs/expression/enum.Term.html)

`Term`[,](https://docs.rs/expression/enum.Operand.html)

`Operand`[,](https://docs.rs/struct.Id.html)

`Id`[, and](https://docs.rs/struct.Selector.html)

`Selector`[.](https://docs.rs/globset/0.4.18/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/globset/glob/struct.Glob.html)

`Glob`[§](https://docs.rs#representation)Representation

Specificity is represented as a 4-tuple `(a, b, c, l)`, which is compared
in lexicographic order, meaning that components are compared in sequence:

- `a`– number of segments with literals only, e.g.- `src`,- `main.rs`.
- `b`– number of segments with single-wildcards, e.g.- `*`,- `?`,- `[abc]`.
- `c`– number of segments with double-wildcards, compared in reverse.
- `l`– number of literals across all segments.

[§](https://docs.rs#atoms)Atoms

In a [ Segment](https://docs.rs/specificity/segment/struct.Segment.html), atoms are combined with

[- the structural component](https://docs.rs/struct.Specificity.html#method.min_sum_len)

`Specificity::min_sum_len``a`, `b`, or `c` is assigned by taking the minimum
across all atoms in the segment, whereas the length component `l` receives
the sum across all atoms in the segment.[§](https://docs.rs#ids-and-selectors)Ids and selectors

The specificity of an [ Id](https://docs.rs/struct.Id.html) or

[is computed by summing the specificities of its components, where the specificity of each component is computed individually and then combined with](https://docs.rs/struct.Selector.html)

`Selector`[. Empty components receive the](https://docs.rs/struct.Specificity.html#method.sum)

`Specificity::sum`[, which is](https://docs.rs/struct.Specificity.html#method.default)

`Specificity::default``(0, 0, 0, 0)`.```
zrs:{git,file}:::{docs}:index.md: # (3, 0, 0, 15)
zrs::::docs:{index,about}.md:     # (2, 0, 0, 12)
zrs:::::index.{md,rst}:           # (1, 0, 0, 8)
zrs:::::{*}:                      # (0, 1, 0, 0)
```
[§](https://docs.rs#expressions)Expressions

An [ Expression](https://docs.rs/struct.Expression.html) is a combination of multiple

[and](https://docs.rs/struct.Id.html)

`Id`[terms, with its specificity computed according to its](https://docs.rs/struct.Selector.html)

`Selector`[:](https://docs.rs/expression/enum.Operator.html)

`Operator`-
`Expression::any`
-
`Expression::all`
-
`Expression::not``(0, 0, 0, 0)`, since a negation is a guard that filters matches but does not select them.

Alternate groups, e.g. `{jpg,png}`, are equivalent to [ Expression::any](https://docs.rs/struct.Expression.html#method.any)
at the

[level and follow the same rules.](https://docs.rs/specificity/segment/enum.Atom.html)

`Atom`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use zrx_id::specificity::ToSpecificity;
use zrx_id::{selector, Expression};
// Create expression and compute specificity
let expr = Expression::any(|expr| {
    expr.with(selector!(location = "**/*.jpg")?)?
        .with(selector!(location = "**/*.png")?)
})?;
assert_eq!(expr.to_specificity(), (0, 1, 1, 4).into());
```

Attempts to convert into a mutable storage reference.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors-1)Errors

The following errors might be returned:

- `Error::Downcast`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-4)Examples

```
use std::any::Any;
use zrx_storage::convert::TryAsStorageMut;
use zrx_storage::Storage;
// Create storage and initial state
let mut storage = Storage::default();
storage.insert("key", 42);
// Obtain mutable type-erased reference
let item: &mut dyn Any = &mut storage;
// Obtain mutable storage reference
let storage = <i32>::try_as_storage_mut(item)?;
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/zrx-store/0.0.10/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/zrx_store/store/item.rs.html#76)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-Value-for-T)

# graph in zrx_graph - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/zrx-graph/0.0.13/zrx_graph/macro.graph.html

```
macro_rules! graph {
    (transitive; $($source:expr => $target:expr),+ $(,)?) => { ... };
    ($($source:expr => $target:expr),+ $(,)?) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Creates a graph from the given pairs.

This macro creates a [ Graph](https://docs.rs/struct.Graph.html) and adds nodes and edges based on the
provided source-target pairs. It’s primarily intended for use in tests and
examples to quickly set up graphs, and is not optimized for performance.
Additionally, the node type must implement

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Copy.html)

`Copy`In case you need a [ Builder](https://docs.rs/struct.Builder.html), e.g. to inspect the graph before building
or to print it to DOT format, use the

[macro.](https://docs.rs/macro.graph_builder.html)

`graph_builder!`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

Create a graph:

```
use zrx_graph::graph;
// Create graph from pairs
let graph = graph! {
    "a" => "b", "a" => "c",
    "b" => "c",
};
```
Create a graph with transitive reachability:

```
use zrx_graph::graph;
// Create graph from pairs
let graph = graph! {
    transitive;
    "a" => "b", "a" => "c",
    "b" => "c",
};
```

---

# graph_builder in zrx_graph - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/zrx-graph/0.0.13/zrx_graph/macro.graph_builder.html

```
macro_rules! graph_builder {
    ($($source:expr => $target:expr),+ $(,)?) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Creates a graph builder from the given pairs.

This macro creates a [ Builder](https://docs.rs/struct.Builder.html) and adds nodes and edges based on the
provided source-target pairs. It’s primarily intended for use in tests and
examples to quickly set up graphs, and is not optimized for performance.
Additionally, the node type must implement

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Copy.html)

`Copy`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use zrx_graph::graph_builder;
// Create graph builder from pairs
let builder = graph_builder! {
    "a" => "b", "a" => "c",
    "b" => "c",
};
```

---
